question: A 33-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 0, at 26 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a routine prenatal examination. Her pregnancy has been uneventful. Physical examination shows a uterus consistent in size with a 26-week gestation. She is given an oral 50-g glucose load; 1 hour later, her serum glucose concentration is 116 mg/dL. Which of the following most likely occurred immediately after the entrance of glucose into the patient's pancreatic beta-cells?

options.opc: Increased expression of hexokinase I mRNA

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Glucose" -> "Entrance into pancreatic beta-cells" -> "Generation of adenosine triphosphate" -> "Exocytosis of insulin granules" -> 80% CHAIN: "Glucose" -> "Entrance into pancreatic beta-cells" -> "Depolarization of beta-cell membrane" -> "Exocytosis of insulin granules" -> 75% CHAIN: "Glucose" -> "Entrance into pancreatic beta-cells" -> "Closure of membranous potassium channels" -> "Depolarization of beta-cell membrane" -> "Exocytosis of insulin granules" -> 80%
analysis: Upon the entrance of glucose into the patient's pancreatic beta-cells, the glucose is metabolized leading to the generation of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). This ATP generation subsequently closes membranous potassium channels, leading to depolarization of the beta-cell membrane and ultimately triggering exocytosis of insulin granules.
